# Native wrapper (Capacitor 8): architecture and open items

**Status:** scaffolded 2026-10-28 on `feature/accounts`; generated by Claude Sonnet 5.5 via Claude Code at T.P's request. **Human review required.** Not built or run on any device or emulator: the machine had no JDK, Android SDK or macOS. Addresses the "no native wrapper" gap (row 1) of the [store-readiness audit](store-readiness-audit-2026-10-28.md); human steps are in [NATIVE.md](../../apps/plan-b-mvp/web/NATIVE.md).

## Architecture

- `apps/plan-b-mvp/web/` stays the Vite + React shell. `capacitor.config.ts` (appId `au.reroute.app`, a placeholder to confirm; `webDir: dist`; Android scheme `https`, iOS scheme `reroute`) packages `dist` into `android/` and `ios/`.
- The legacy `app.js`, `offline.js`, `app.css`, icons and vendor files are normally served by Flask next to `dist`. `scripts/prepare-native.mjs` copies them into `dist` for the bundle. `sw.js` is not bundled (WKWebView custom schemes cannot run service workers; registration already has a `.catch`).
- The app calls `fetch("/api/...")`. `src/native/api.js` rewrites those to `VITE_API_BASE` on native only (build-time, set by `npm run build:native`).
- `src/main.jsx` calls `initNative()` only when `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()`. Every adapter in `src/native/` is a dynamic import, so the browser never downloads them. Measured: main chunk 124.20 to 124.37 kB gzip (+0.17 kB). Browser checked at 390x844: no console errors, no native chunk requested, geolocation untouched.
- Capacitor 8 uses Swift Package Manager for iOS (`ios/App/CapApp-SPM`), so CocoaPods is not needed. `cap add ios` worked on Windows; building needs a Mac.

## Adapters (`web/src/native/`)

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `platform.js` | `isNative()`, `platform()`; the only eager file |
| `index.js` | startup, adds `native` classes to `<html>`, loads the others |
| `api.js` | relative `/api` to `VITE_API_BASE` |
| `geolocation.js` | replaces `navigator.geolocation` and the geolocation permission query with `@capacitor/geolocation` (native prompt; `app.js` unchanged) |
| `network.js` | re-dispatches `online`/`offline` window events from `@capacitor/network` (feeds the existing offline banner) |
| `deeplinks.js` | `appUrlOpen` for `https://<domain>/...` and `reroute://...` to the router (history + `popstate`), closes the in-app browser (OAuth return), Android back button; emits `reroute:deeplink` |
| `share.js` | `navigator.share` to the native share sheet (the existing "Share with other apps" button then appears and works) |
| `chrome.js` | status bar style and colour follow `data-theme`, Android edge-to-edge overlay, hides the native splash, iOS keyboard accessory bar off |
| `push.js` | `enablePush()` registers for FCM/APNs and POSTs the token; **not wired to the UI**: call it from the existing notification button on native |
| `auth.js` | `signIn("apple" or "google", cfg)` via `@capgo/capacitor-social-login`; **not wired**: the accounts screen owner calls it and sends the `idToken` to the server |

Haptics: `src/haptics.js` already routed to `@capacitor/haptics` (light/medium/heavy impact, selection, error notification) when native and to `navigator.vibrate` on the web; unchanged. The optional iOS-Safari `<input switch>` tick was skipped (undocumented trick, not needed in the native shell).

## Plugins and why

app (deep links, back), browser (OAuth in-app browser), geolocation, haptics, push-notifications (APNs/FCM; audit blocker 5), local-notifications (installed, unused: departure reminders later), network, preferences (installed, unused: native storage for tokens later, as WebView localStorage can be evicted), share, splash-screen, status-bar, keyboard, device (installed, unused), `@capgo/capacitor-social-login` 8.7.5 (Apple and Google in one maintained plugin, peer `@capacitor/core >=8`; `@codetrix-studio/capacitor-google-auth` only supports Capacitor 6 and `@capacitor-community/apple-sign-in` 7+, so neither was used). `@capacitor/filesystem` not needed. Dev: `@capacitor/cli`, `@capacitor/assets`, `sharp`, `typescript` (needed to read `capacitor.config.ts`). Remove unused plugins before release to shrink the permission surface if a reviewer asks.

## Platform config

- **Android:** compile/target SDK 36, min SDK 24 (Capacitor template). Permissions: INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, ACCESS_COARSE/FINE_LOCATION, POST_NOTIFICATIONS, VIBRATE. No background location (navigation runs in the foreground; if added later it needs a Play declaration and a prominent disclosure). `usesCleartextTraffic=false`, `network_security_config.xml` (HTTPS, system CAs), `allowBackup=false`. App Links intent filter with `autoVerify` for `reroute.example` (TODO real domain) and the `reroute://` scheme. Adaptive icon, mipmaps and splash generated from `favicon.svg`.
- **iOS:** deployment target 15. `Info.plist`: `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`, `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption=false`, `reroute` URL scheme. `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`: no tracking; collected data precise location (not linked), email, name, user ID and device ID (push token) linked, all for app functionality; required-reason APIs UserDefaults CA92.1, FileTimestamp C617.1, SystemBootTime 35F9.1, DiskSpace E174.1. `App.entitlements`: `aps-environment`, `applinks:reroute.example` (TODO), Sign in with Apple. These need a paid Apple Developer team; delete the keys to test on a free personal team. The files were wired into `project.pbxproj` by hand: open the project once in Xcode and confirm they appear in the App target.
- **Safe areas:** `viewport-fit=cover` is set and `app.css` pads with `env(safe-area-inset-*)` on the header, scroll areas, footers and sheets. Android 15+ edge-to-edge relies on the status-bar overlay plus those insets; confirm the top inset on a real Android 15 device.

## Contracts for the server owner (not implemented here; `server.py` untouched)

1. **CORS:** allow origins `https://localhost` (Android) and `reroute://localhost` (iOS), methods GET/POST/OPTIONS, headers `Content-Type` and `Authorization`. If sessions use cookies, they need `SameSite=None; Secure` and may still be dropped by WKWebView; prefer bearer tokens for native.
2. **`POST /api/push/native-register`**, body `{"token": "<fcm or apns token>", "platform": "ios" | "android", "watch": <same object as /api/push/subscribe, or null>}`; return `200 {"ok": true}`, `400` on bad input; rate-limit like `/api/push/subscribe`. Sending via FCM HTTP v1 for both platforms (upload the APNs key to Firebase) is simplest. Add an unregister endpoint for logout.
3. **`/.well-known/assetlinks.json`** (`application/json`, no redirect):

```json
[{"relation": ["delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls"], "target": {"namespace": "android_app", "package_name": "au.reroute.app", "sha256_cert_fingerprints": ["<SHA-256 of the Play App Signing certificate; add the upload key for sideloaded tests>"]}}]
```

4. **`/.well-known/apple-app-site-association`** (served as `application/json`, no file extension, no redirect):

```json
{"applinks": {"details": [{"appIDs": ["<TEAM_ID>.au.reroute.app"], "components": [{"/": "/*"}]}]}, "webcredentials": {"apps": ["<TEAM_ID>.au.reroute.app"]}}
```

5. OAuth return: redirect the in-app browser to `https://<domain>/auth/callback?...` (App Link) or `reroute://auth/callback?...`; `deeplinks.js` maps both to the same path.

## Still needs a Mac, accounts or secrets

Build and run on iOS (Mac, Xcode); Apple Developer Program (US$99) for signing, push, Associated Domains, Sign in with Apple and TestFlight; Google Play developer account (US$25) and upload keystore; Firebase project with `google-services.json` and `GoogleService-Info.plist`; production domain and the well-known files; Google Maps keys per platform (the web key is HTTP-referrer restricted and the bundled origin is `https://localhost` / `reroute://localhost`, so add those referrers or use a native-only key; audit row 8); Google and Apple OAuth client IDs; on-device testing of every adapter; screenshots, listing text, privacy labels and the Data safety form.

## Known limits

- `watchPosition` ids are shim-local; `maximumAge` caching is whatever the plugin does.
- Service worker features (offline shell, web push) are off in the bundle; offline maps use IndexedDB and still work.
- `allowNavigation` in `capacitor.config.ts` reads `VITE_API_BASE` at `cap sync` time; keep it set when syncing.
- Social login needs real client IDs; unused until wired.
